title: Add Plausible analytics script
description: Adds the Plausible analytics script to the app's `<head>` by wrapping `page_chat()` in a `tagList()` with a `tags$head()` block.

title: Install the packages dependencies compile with
description:
Today's noon deploy, the first with the tidyverse, failed when rsconnect captured the dependencies: renv refused to snapshot because `progress` wasn't installed, which readxl and vroom only need to compile from source (`LinkingTo`), like `cpp11` before (#14). Of the 139 packages in the app's dependency tree, `cpp11` and `progress` are the only `LinkingTo` packages that aren't installed as ordinary dependencies.

Instead of listing them in `extra-packages`, a step installs whatever is missing of the `LinkingTo` packages of everything installed, so a new dependency can't cause the same failure.

title: Make the tidyverse available to the agent
description:
The R code the agent writes runs in the app's own R installation. On Connect Cloud, that has only the packages rsconnect records from `DESCRIPTION` and the app's code: dplyr and tibble, but not ggplot2, tidyr, readr, purrr, stringr, forcats or lubridate, so code using them would fail when deployed (laptops tend to have them, which hides it).

- `tidyverse` is in `Imports`, so rsconnect records it and its packages, and the Deploy workflow installs them; the meta-package itself, because LLMs often write `library(tidyverse)`
- `instructions.md` tells the agent: "The tidyverse is installed; prefer it for data wrangling and plots."

title: Send OPENAI_API_KEY with every deploy
description:
The first deploy from GitHub removed `OPENAI_API_KEY` from the app. rsconnect 1.11.2 sends the app's variables with every deploy to Connect Cloud (`secrets = cloudSecrets(deployment$envVars)` in `prepareContent.connectCloudClient()`), and Connect Cloud replaces the app's variables with them; without `envVars` that's an empty list.

- `deploy.R` passes `envVars = "OPENAI_API_KEY"` again, and refuses to deploy without the key, so a deploy can't remove it
- The Deploy workflow gets it from the repository secret `OPENAI_API_KEY`; pull requests, which don't deploy, don't need it

Needs the repository secret `OPENAI_API_KEY` before merging.

title: Install cpp11 in the Deploy workflow
description: The first deploy from GitHub to the jeroenjanssens account logged in and found the app, then failed when rsconnect captured the R dependencies: renv refused to snapshot because `cpp11` wasn't installed. roxygen2, systemfonts and textshaping need it only to build from source, so the binaries CI installs don't bring it; laptops usually have it. The workflow now installs it with the other extra packages.

title: Read secrets from .env when running locally
description:
`agent.R` reads `.env` when the file exists, so running the app locally needs no `readRenviron()`, and `deploy.R` gets the Connect Cloud credentials and `CONNECT_CLOUD_APP_ID` from it when deploying from a laptop. `.env` is ignored by Git and isn't among the files `deploy.R` uploads; on Connect Cloud the secrets are the app's Variables. The README explains both.

Deploying from a laptop this way created the app on the `jeroenjanssens` account (`01a1684c-6747-bffe-4c7e-cd5eac644087`), now the repository variable `CONNECT_CLOUD_APP_ID`.

title: Publish to the jeroenjanssens account
description:
deploy.R publishes to Connect Cloud's `jeroenjanssens` account instead of `posit`, which means a new app there.

- The app's id comes from the repository variable `CONNECT_CLOUD_APP_ID` instead of being hard-coded
- Without it, a deploy started by hand creates the app (`devrel-agent`, titled "devrel agent") and prints its id and URL; a scheduled run refuses, so the nightly run can't create a new app every night
- The workflow installs velocirepo 1.3.1

After merging: run Deploy by hand, set the printed id with `gh variable set CONNECT_CLOUD_APP_ID --body <id>`, and add `OPENAI_API_KEY` to the new app's Variables on Connect Cloud. The client credentials need publish permission on the `jeroenjanssens` account.

title: Deploy nightly with fresh data
description:
Implements posit-dev/velocirepo's `docs/design/2026-10-devrel-agent-deploy.md`.

At noon UTC, two and a half hours after devrel-io's nightly fetch, the Deploy workflow:

1. checks out devrel-io's latest commit (no history; `velocirepo.toml` and `velocirepo/data` only)
2. exports it with velocirepo 1.2.0: `data/velocirepo.duckdb` and `data/data-dict.yaml`
3. validates the dictionary with data-dict (errors stop the deploy, warnings don't)
4. runs `deploy.R`: refuses data more than 3 days old, prewarms commons' context index, logs in with Connect Cloud client credentials and deploys

If a step fails, nothing is deployed and the previous version keeps running. Pull requests run everything but the deploy. By hand (Actions → Deploy → Run workflow), it deploys now, an older devrel-io commit (`devrel-io-ref`), or only checks (`deploy: false`).

`deploy.R` no longer sends `OPENAI_API_KEY` (`envVars`): the key is set once in the app's Content Settings → Variables on Connect Cloud, so it never passes through GitHub. Prewarming calls no model, so CI needs no API key.

Before merging:

- [ ] Add `OPENAI_API_KEY` to the app's Content Settings → Variables on Connect Cloud, deploy once from a laptop with this `deploy.R`, and check the agent still answers
- [ ] Create a Connect Cloud client credential at https://login.posit.cloud/identity/credentials and add `CONNECT_CLOUD_CLIENT_ID` and `CONNECT_CLOUD_CLIENT_SECRET` as repository secrets
- [ ] After merging, run the workflow by hand and check the deployed app (`SELECT * FROM meta` gives yesterday)

title: Build the database and data dictionary with velocirepo export
description:
velocirepo 1.2.0 writes everything the agent reads: `velocirepo export --data-dict` writes `data/velocirepo.duckdb`, a standalone database, and `data/data-dict.yaml`, a data dictionary generated from the schema, the data and the `[data_dict]` section of devrel-io's `velocirepo.toml` (posit-dev/devrel-io#5).

- `etl/build-db.R` and the hand-written `dictionaries/devrel.data-dict.yaml` are gone; the README's "Run it locally" explains the export and how to start the app
- The agent gets the `targets` table, which says which sources cover a project
- `deploy.R` ships the new files
- The evals use `events.user`, as velocirepo names it, and the targets are re-authored against the snapshot of 2026-10-21; 54 of the 55 targets computed the same on the old and the new database before that, the other differing only in the order of a tie
- `inst/devrel-io/`, the clone the export reads, is ignored

Not changed: the rubrics of q04 (expects that there's no star data) and q10 (a measurement change on 2026-06-23), which the data repair of 2026-10-20 made wrong.

title: Fix conversation bleed: build the agent per Shiny session
description:
## Problem

The app shared one `devrel_agent` across all Shiny sessions. A commons agent holds a single conversation, so concurrent users were writing into the same one: each user's questions became part of the model's context when answering the other, and their exchanges were saved into each other's history.

## Fix

Build the agent per session. The read-only DuckDB connection stays shared — Shiny handles one event at a time, so sessions never query it concurrently.

This is a correctness fix, not a performance one. If session-startup cost is a concern, we'll address it separately.
